newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine benchmark T-bill rate down at 11.48 pct.
newsitem.headline: Philippine benchmark T-bill rate down at 11.48 pct.

text.p: The Philippines' bellwether 91-day Treasury bill rate slipped to 11.48 percent from 11.70 percent registered in the previous auction, the Bureau of Treasury said on Monday.
The auction committee awarded one billion pesos worth of three-month bills, rejecting 995 million pesos of tenders received from financial institutions.
Average rates for 182- and 364-day bills fell significantly due to oversubscription.
The six-month bill yield rates fell to 11.852 percent from 12.32 percent posted two weeks ago, while one-year bill rates fell to 12.25 percent from 12.735 percent.
The auction committee suspended the weekly auction last Monday due to the leaders' summit of the Asia Pacific Economic Cooperation which was held in Subic free port, just north of Manila.
"This whetted the appetite of banks for T-bills," one trader said.
A total of 5.53 billion pesos worth of bids were received for the six-month bills, while 11.11 billion pesos were tendered for the one-year bills.
